profile.reading: This OpenStreetMap node, tagged simply Windstream, sits in Tulsa County, Oklahoma, though no street address is recorded for it and no operator-published facility page describing it could be located this session. Windstream Holdings is a US telecom and broadband carrier formed in 2006 through the merger of Alltel wireline division and Valor Communications Group, itself built from wireline assets Verizon had divested, and headquartered in Little Rock, Arkansas. Over the following decade Windstream expanded through a long series of acquisitions, including CT Communications, D&E Communications, Iowa Telecom, NuVox, PAETEC, EarthLink, and Broadview Networks, along with a 2010 purchase of Hosted Solutions, a North Carolina-based managed hosting and colocation company that gave Windstream a distinct data center product line built around facilities in Cary, Raleigh, and Charlotte, North Carolina, and Boston, Massachusetts, none of which were in Oklahoma. Windstream filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 2019 and emerged in 2020 with reduced debt, and more recently completed a merger into Uniti Group Inc around August 2025, confirmed by windstream.com now redirecting to the consumer Kinetic brand site and windstreambusiness.com data center solutions page now redirecting to Uniti own solutions site. No source reviewed this session ties Oklahoma or Tulsa specifically to Windstream legacy incumbent local exchange carrier territory or to its former Hosted Solutions data center product line, and the OpenStreetMap tag itself was added in April 2026 as part of a large, semi-automated batch edit citing generic sourcing rather than a documented site survey, so this record facility type, current status, and even its basic existence as a data center rather than ordinary network infrastructure remain genuinely unconfirmed.

reading.body:
This record marks a data center tagged to Windstream in Tulsa County, Oklahoma via OpenStreetMap in April 2026 as part of a large semi-automated batch edit, but no operator-published facility page, street address, or confirmation of current status could be located. Windstream Holdings, formed in 2006 and headquartered in Arkansas, operated a dedicated data center product line through its 2010 acquisition of Hosted Solutions, but those facilities were in North Carolina and Massachusetts, not Oklahoma, and the company merged into Uniti Group around August 2025, making the currency of any Windstream-branded infrastructure uncertain. The tag itself carries weaker provenance than a documented site survey, so whether this location functions as a data center, remains operational, or ever housed AI-relevant compute cannot be confirmed from available sources.

Oklahoma has nine mapped data center facilities on record but zero published megawatt specifications from any operator in the state, so this campus, like all others there, does not appear in any public capacity disclosure. Without published power consumption, IT load, or facility specifications, no calculation of rack count, accelerator density, or AI hosting capability is possible.

This record should be treated as unconfirmed and flagged for ground-truth verification before inclusion in any assessment of regional compute capacity or AI infrastructure ranking.
